items.html: Upper ones, which are the vowel Holam, and a middle one, such as Shuruk, and all the rest are lower ones: (54) For three lights served in Nekudim. The first is the vapour of the Tabur, which is the Peh of the first Rosh, called YESHSUT; and this light is called Holam, since it illuminates above the letters. This is because the first Rosh is not reckoned as the light of the Nekudot proper, but only as a root, and even at the time of Gadlut [greatness] it does not join into one with its AHP, which is the GAR of Nekudim (and see above in the Inner Light, page 423, the passage beginning “The Holam”). The second light is the vapour of the Yesod, which is the inner ZON that illuminate the GAR of Nekudim — Vav to Ima, Yod to Aba — as above in the words of the ARI, page 423, item 31. And this light is called Shuruk, because it illuminates inside the vessels of AVI. And the third light is the light bestowed from the Peh of Nekudim downward upon the ZAT of Nekudim, which are drawn from the Parsa by means of the coupling of Gadlut (as above in the Inner Light, 424, the passage beginning “And seven Nekudot”). They are therefore the lower Nekudot that are beneath the letters, that is, they are drawn from beneath the vessels of the upper one, for the Parsa is the final conclusion of the toes of the feet of SAG of AK.
